elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall ..." — covers both expiry and termination, at Agreement and Order Form level, for any reason.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: "(a) at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six months". The request condition is unqualified and available on any expiry or termination, so it does not fail the after-every-covered-event test.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: "... for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "(b) within thirty days after that expiry or termination, return all Customer Data" — the 30-day clock is anchored to the termination/expiry event, not to a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: "return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: "(c) after that return, delete Customer Data from its systems and certify the deletion in writing" — deletion and certification expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted trigger language: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Up to six months of assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty days after that expiry or termination, return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format" satisfies export within 30 days.

reasons: The single inserted paragraph delivers every preferred element in operative language: expiry-or-termination trigger for any reason, up to six months' assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, 30-day return of all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format measured from the termination event, and written certification of deletion after that return.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a concise new clause for a genuinely missing obligation, tracks the model language without extras (no survival tail, no at-own-expense or damages add-ons, no procedural boilerplate), and no existing words in 10.1, 10.2 or 16.5 were deleted or paraphrased.

Intent preserved: 10.1's "any agreed transition period" access wind-down and 10.2's Deliverable-delivery and Fee-refund mechanics survive without contradiction; the new clause adds an entitlement rather than displacing them. The pre-existing dangling reference in 16.5 to a non-existent Section 11 is untouched by this redline and is correctly left to a housekeeping pass rather than expanded here.

Housekeeping only (no defect in substance): the rendered insertion carries no section number although the rationale describes it as a new 10.3 — number it 10.3 on execution so the clause sits cleanly in the termination section and can be cross-referenced.
Fallback is also fully met, so the fallback offered in the margin comment is a genuine retreat position rather than a promise of something the draft lacks.
